title: Best Museums for Kids in Singapore 2026 — Interactive & Educational
excerpt: Singapore's museums are world-class — and many are surprisingly kid-friendly. From hands-on science centres to immersive art experiences, here's our curated guide to the best museums in Singapore that kids will actually enjoy.
content:
Singapore punches well above its weight when it comes to museums, and the island has invested heavily in making its cultural institutions genuinely engaging for children. Gone are the days of 'look but don't touch' — today's best Singapore museums are built around interactivity, play, and discovery. We visited over a dozen museums across the island with kids aged 3–12 to find the ones that earned genuine enthusiasm (not just polite tolerance). Here's our guide to the best museums for kids in Singapore in 2026.

1. ArtScience Museum — Marina Bay Sands

Best for: Ages 3–12 | Location: Marina Bay Sands | Duration: 1.5–3 hours | Price: From SGD 19 adult / SGD 14 child ($14 / $10 USD)

The ArtScience Museum at Marina Bay Sands is arguably the most kid-friendly museum in Singapore. The iconic lotus-shaped building houses the permanent FUTURE WORLD exhibition — a digital art playground created in collaboration with teamLab that's essentially a giant interactive art installation designed for children.

FUTURE WORLD is divided into several zones: 'Nature' where kids can colour in pictures of animals that come to life on massive projection screens; 'Town' where children can build cars, houses, and buildings out of giant soft blocks and watch them become part of a projected cityscape; 'Park' with interactive digital plants and flowers that bloom and scatter when touched; and 'Space' featuring a mesmerising digital light sculpture that responds to movement. The entire experience is tactile, visual, and joyfully chaotic — kids run from zone to zone creating, touching, and exploring.

Kid-approved: 'The colouring section was the best! I drew a fish, scanned it, and it swam away in the ocean on the wall. I made three more fish and they all swam together.' — Maya, age 6, Singapore.

Parent tip: Book tickets online — walk-up queues can be 30+ minutes on weekends. The museum is busiest 11am–3pm; aim for a 10am entry. The gift shop has some excellent art-and-craft kits that make great souvenirs. Combine with a visit to the Marina Bay Sands SkyPark for sunset views — same location, different ticket.

2. KidsSTOP™ — Science Centre Singapore

Best for: Ages 18 months–8 years | Location: Jurong East | Duration: 2–3 hours | Price: SGD 10 per person ($7.50 USD)

KidsSTOP is Singapore's first dedicated children's science centre, and it's a masterclass in early childhood STEM education through play. The centre is divided into four zones — Imagine, Experience, Discover, and Dream — each targeting different developmental stages and interests. Toddlers have a dedicated soft-play area with sensory walls, ball pits, and simple cause-effect exhibits. Preschoolers can explore a kid-sized supermarket, construction site, and hospital — each stocked with realistic tools and props that encourage role-play.

The highlight for most kids is the 'Flight and Space' zone with a mini aeroplane cockpit they can 'fly,' complete with sound effects, blinking buttons, and a viewscreen showing Singapore from the sky. There's also a water play zone where kids can experiment with dams, pumps, and water flow. The entire facility is clean, well-maintained, and staffed by patient educators who engage with children rather than just supervising.

Parent tip: KidsSTOP operates in two-hour sessions — book your session in advance online. The centre is inside the Science Centre Singapore complex, so you can pair it with the main Science Centre or the Snow City attraction next door for a full day out. Food options are limited to the Science Centre food court — pack snacks. Free lockers are available.

Parent verdict: 'KidsSTOP was the highlight of our three-week Singapore trip. Our 4-year-old spent an hour in the mini supermarket 'working as a cashier.' She still talks about the aeroplane cockpit. The two-hour session felt perfectly timed — any longer and she would've crashed.' — Tomoko, mother of one, Japan.

3. National Museum of Singapore — Children's Season

Best for: Ages 4–10 | Location: Stamford Road (City Hall) | Duration: 1–2 hours | Price: Free–SGD 15 per child (varies by program)

Singapore's oldest museum might not sound like a kid-friendly destination, but the National Museum has invested heavily in making its galleries accessible to children. The permanent 'Singapore Gallery' has a dedicated children's trail with activity sheets, interactive displays, and touch-screen exhibits that tell Singapore's story from a 14th-century fishing village to a modern metropolis in ways that engage young minds.

The real draw, however, is the museum's Children's Season — a biannual program (June and December) that transforms the museum into a wonderland of special exhibitions, workshops, storytelling sessions, and hands-on activities designed specifically for children. Past editions have included 'A Journey Through Little Red Dot' (a storytelling-based exploration of Singapore's history), 'Mystery at the Museum' (a detective-style treasure hunt), and 'Time Travellers' Workshop' (where kids create artefacts from different historical periods).

Parent tip: Check the museum's website for the current Children's Season schedule before visiting. Most Children's Season activities require advance registration (they fill up fast). The museum cafe, Food for Thought, has a decent kids' menu and is reasonably priced. The museum is a 5-minute walk from Dhoby Ghaut MRT.

4. Lee Kong Chian Natural History Museum — NUS

Best for: Ages 5–12 | Location: National University of Singapore (Kent Ridge) | Duration: 1.5–2 hours | Price: SGD 16 adult / SGD 9 child ($12 / $7 USD)

Dinosaur-obsessed kids (and really, what kid isn't?) will lose their minds at the Lee Kong Chian Natural History Museum. The museum's centrepiece is the 'Three Sisters' — three massive diplodocid dinosaur skeletons (Prince, Apollonia, and Twinky) that are among the most complete sauropod fossils ever discovered. The skeletons dominate the museum's main hall and are visible from every level.

Beyond the dinosaurs, the museum houses over 560,000 specimens organised across 12 thematic zones covering Southeast Asian biodiversity — from the deep sea to the rainforest canopy. Interactive exhibits let kids touch real fossils, examine specimens under digital microscopes, and learn about evolution, extinction, and conservation. The 'Heritage of Nature' gallery showcases the region's most spectacular specimens, including a whale skeleton suspended from the ceiling.

Kid-approved: 'The big dinosaur skeletons are SO COOL! They're like the ones in Jurassic Park but real. I learned that the long neck ones ate plants and the T-Rex ones ate meat. Can we come back tomorrow?' — Leo, age 7, Australia.

Parent tip: The museum is located on the NUS campus — a 15-minute walk from Kent Ridge MRT. Parking is available but limited on weekdays. Combine with a walk around the beautiful NUS campus (lots of green space for kids to run) or a visit to the nearby West Coast Park. The museum gift shop has excellent fossil-themed souvenirs. Guided tours (free with admission) run daily at 11am and 2pm.

5. Trick Eye Museum — Sentosa

Best for: Ages 4–12 (and Instagram-loving adults) | Location: Sentosa Island (Resorts World Sentosa) | Duration: 1–1.5 hours | Price: SGD 25 adult / SGD 20 child ($19 / $15 USD)

The Trick Eye Museum on Sentosa is an optical illusion museum where everything is designed to be touched, climbed on, and photographed. The museum features over 100 3D paintings and optical illusion installations — think giant waterfalls you can pretend to push back, shark cages you can climb into, and flying carpets you can straddle. The entire experience is built around creating the perfect photo, and the museum provides 'photo spot' markers on the floor showing where to stand for the best illusion effect.

Kids love the interactivity — everything in the museum is fair game for touching, posing, and playing. The 'Love in Singapore' zone is cute for family photos, the 'Adventure' zone has a jungle theme with giant animals, and the 'Winter' zone lets kids pretend to ice-skate (no actual skates — just the illusion of it).

Parent tip: Go early (the museum opens at 10am) to avoid crowds — popular installations can have photo queues later in the day. The museum is inside Resorts World Sentosa, so combine with Universal Studios, S.E.A. Aquarium, or Sentosa beaches. Book on Klook for discounted tickets. Bring a phone with a good camera — the museum's provided photo service charges extra for prints.

6. Asian Civilisations Museum — Family Sundays

Best for: Ages 5–12 | Location: Empress Place (Raffles Place) | Duration: 1–2 hours | Price: Free for Singaporeans / SGD 12 adults, kids free ($9 USD)

The Asian Civilisations Museum might sound dry for kids, but its weekly Family Sunday program makes it genuinely engaging. Every Sunday, the museum runs free family-friendly activities — storytelling sessions in the galleries, craft workshops inspired by the collections, dress-up corners where kids can try on traditional costumes, and gallery trails with activity sheets. The museum's permanent collection — covering the art, culture, and history of Asia — is presented with plenty of multimedia interactives and touch-screen displays.

The riverfront location is a bonus — the museum overlooks the Singapore River with views of Boat Quay, and the outdoor area is perfect for a post-museum picnic. The museum's restaurant, Empress, has a Sunday brunch that's family-friendly (kids eat free with paying adults).

Parent tip: Family Sunday activities run 10am–4pm. Arrive early to sign up for the craft workshops (they cap attendance). The museum is a 5-minute walk from Raffles Place MRT. Free lockers and stroller parking are available at the entrance.

7. Children's Museum Singapore (Formerly Playeum)

Best for: Ages 2–8 | Location: Coleman Street (City Hall) | Duration: 1.5–2.5 hours | Price: Free (registration required)

Singapore's newest dedicated children's museum is a hands-on wonderland for younger kids. The Children's Museum Singapore (CMSG) replaced the beloved Playeum and expanded into a larger space in the historic Old School building near City Hall. The museum features rotating thematic exhibitions — past themes have included 'Imagine a Garden' (exploring nature and sustainability through play), 'Imagine a World' (a miniature city kids can build and rebuild), and 'Imagine a Home' (exploring different types of homes across Singapore).

The permanent exhibit area includes a 'Sensory Play Studio' with tactile walls, light tables, and sound installations; a 'Construction Zone' with giant foam blocks and building materials; and a 'Quiet Corner' for overwhelmed little ones with books, puzzles, and dimmed lighting. The museum also runs workshops on weekends — everything from clay sculpting to simple coding for preschoolers.

Parent tip: CMSG is free but requires online registration — book at least a week in advance, especially for weekends. Sessions are capped to prevent overcrowding. The museum is a 3-minute walk from City Hall MRT. The nearby Fort Canning Park is perfect for a post-museum run-around. Food options along Coleman Street are limited — the museum has a small cafe, but you're better off walking 5 minutes to the Funan Mall for a proper meal.

Quick Comparison

  • Best for toddlers (2–4): Children's Museum Singapore — free, sensory-rich, age-appropriate
  • Best for preschoolers (4–6): KidsSTOP — dedicated science play centre with role-play zones
  • Best for primary school (6–12): ArtScience Museum FUTURE WORLD — digital art + interactive installations
  • Best for dinosaur fans: Lee Kong Chian Natural History Museum — real dinosaur skeletons
  • Best for photo-obsessed families: Trick Eye Museum — 3D illusions, perfect for social media
  • Best free option: Children's Museum Singapore — completely free with registration
  • Best for rainy days: ArtScience Museum (indoor, air-conditioned, spacious)

Practical Tips for Museum-Going with Kids in Singapore

  • Book online in advance: Almost every museum on this list offers online booking, and some (KidsSTOP, CMSG) require it. Booking ahead also secures the best time slots and often gives a small discount.
  • Use the MRT: Every museum on this list is within walking distance of an MRT station. Singapore's public transport is reliable, clean, and stroller-friendly.
  • Bring a refillable water bottle: Singapore's tap water is safe to drink. Most museums have water coolers. Buying bottled water at museum cafes adds up quickly.
  • Check for free entry days: Many Singapore museums offer free admission to Singaporeans and PRs. The National Museum and Asian Civilisations Museum have free entry for kids year-round.
  • Look for the Museum Roundtable pass: A SGD 20 pass gives you entry to 8 museums over 30 days — excellent value if you're visiting Singapore for a week or more.
  • Sunscreen + hat: Even though you're museum-hopping, the walk between MRT stations and museums in Singapore's tropical heat requires sun protection.

Our verdict: Singapore's museum scene for kids is among the best in Asia. The ArtScience Museum's FUTURE WORLD is the must-do — it's genuinely unique and kids of all ages adore it. KidsSTOP is the best option for families with younger children (toddlers to early primary). And the Children's Museum Singapore proves that free can still be world-class. Budget at least one full museum day on your next Singapore family trip — and remember to book ahead.
author: Kids Activities Asia Team
